chapters.title: 1. 길동의 가족과 마음
chapters.text:
옛날에 홍 판서가 살았습니다. 홍 판서는 나라의 일을 했습니다. 홍 판서에게는 아들이 두 명 있었습니다. 한 아이는 인형이고 다른 아이는 길동이었습니다. 인형의 어머니는 유 부인이었습니다. 유 부인은 홍 판서의 아내였습니다. 길동의 어머니는 춘섬이었습니다. 춘섬은 홍 판서의 집에서 일을 했습니다. 인형과 길동의 아버지는 같았지만 어머니는 달랐습니다. 인형은 길동의 형이었습니다.

길동이 태어나기 전에 홍 판서는 꿈을 꾸었습니다. 꿈에서 용을 보았습니다. 용이 홍 판서에게 빨리 왔습니다. 홍 판서는 잠에서 일어난 후에 아주 기뻤습니다. 홍 판서는 생각했습니다.
‘이제 특별한 아이가 태어날 것입니다.’
나중에 춘섬도 홍 판서와 함께 살았습니다. 하지만 춘섬은 유 부인과 같은 아내는 아니었습니다. 춘섬의 신분은 유 부인보다 낮았습니다. 그리고 춘섬의 아들 길동이 태어났습니다. 아기는 특별했습니다. 홍 판서는 아주 기뻤습니다. 하지만 길동의 어머니는 유 부인이 아니었습니다. 그래서 홍 판서는 기뻤지만 마음은 슬펐습니다.

시간이 지났습니다. 길동은 여덟 살이었습니다. 길동은 아주 빨리 배우고 공부도 잘했습니다. 아버지는 길동을 더 사랑했습니다. 하지만 길동의 생활은 힘들었습니다. 사람의 신분은 모두 같지 않았습니다. 홍 판서의 신분은 높았습니다. 춘섬의 신분은 낮았습니다. 길동은 춘섬의 아들이라서 신분이 낮았습니다.

길동에게는 아버지와 형이 있었습니다. 하지만 아버지를 ‘아버지’라고 부를 수 없었습니다. 형도 ‘형’이라고 부를 수 없었습니다. 길동이 아버지를 ‘아버지’라고 불렀습니다. 아버지는 길동에게 화를 냈습니다. 시간이 더 지났습니다. 길동은 열 살이 넘었습니다. 하지만 아직 아버지를 ‘아버지’라고 부를 수 없었습니다. 형도 ‘형’이라고 부를 수 없었습니다. 집에서 여러 사람이 일을 했습니다. 그 사람들도 길동의 신분이 낮아서 길동을 낮게 보았습니다. 길동의 마음은 아주 아팠습니다.

가을 밤이었습니다. 길동은 책을 읽고 있었습니다. 하지만 마음이 슬펐습니다. 길동은 혼자 말했습니다.
“나는 나라를 돕고 싶습니다. 나라의 일을 잘하고 싶습니다. 사람들에게 내 이름도 알리고 싶습니다. 하지만 지금 나는 혼자입니다. 아버지도 있고 형도 있습니다. 그런데 나는 왜 아버지를 ‘아버지’라고 부를 수 없습니까? 왜 형을 ‘형’이라고 부를 수 없습니까? 마음이 너무 아픕니다.”

길동은 밖으로 나갔습니다. 칼을 들고 연습을 했습니다. 아버지도 밖에 있었습니다. 아버지는 길동을 보고 불렀습니다.
“밤이 늦었습니다. 왜 아직 안 잡니까?”
길동이 대답했습니다.
“저도 사람입니다. 그런데 왜 저는 다른 사람과 같지 않습니까? 왜 저는 사람도 아닙니까?”

아버지는 길동의 마음을 알았습니다. 하지만 다시 길동에게 화를 냈습니다.
“무슨 말입니까?”
길동은 아버지 앞에서 다시 말했습니다.
“저는 부모님에게 고맙습니다. 하지만 저는 아주 슬픕니다. 제 아버지가 앞에 있습니다. 그런데 저는 아버지를 ‘아버지’라고 부를 수 없습니다. 형도 ‘형’이라고 부를 수 없습니다.”

길동은 울었습니다. 아버지의 마음도 아팠습니다. 하지만 아버지는 걱정했습니다.
‘지금 길동에게 좋은 말을 하면 나중에 길동이 내 말을 안 들을까?’
그래서 아버지는 길동에게 아주 화를 냈습니다.
“다른 집에도 너와 같은 아이가 있습니다. 그 아이의 어머니도 신분이 낮습니다. 그 말은 안 됩니다. 다시 듣고 싶지 않습니다.”

길동은 대답할 수 없었습니다. 계속 울었습니다. 아버지는 길동에게 말했습니다.
“이제 나가세요.”
길동은 방으로 돌아갔습니다. 하지만 마음은 아직 아주 슬펐습니다.

grammar_links.context_en: 에 marks 옛날 as the time when Minister Hong lived.
가 marks Minister Hong as the person who lived.
-았- places Minister Hong's life in the past.
-습니다 closes the narration as a formal polite statement.
는 establishes Minister Hong as the topic: the sentence tells us what he did.
의 connects 나라 to 일: work concerned with the country's affairs.
을 marks 일 as the work Minister Hong carried out.
The past marker in 했습니다 places his work before the time of narration. 하다 becomes 했다.
했습니다 ends the statement in the narration's formal polite style.
에게 identifies Minister Hong as the person who had the sons. With 있었습니다, the sentence means that he had two sons.
는 follows 에게 and makes Minister Hong the topic: as for Minister Hong, he had two sons.
이 marks the sons as what existed in Minister Hong's family; English expresses this relationship as ‘he had sons’.
-었- places Minister Hong's having two sons in the past.
-습니다 ends the past statement in the chapter's formal polite narrative style.
는 marks one child as the topic and contrasts him with the other child.
The copula identifies the first child as Inhyeong.
-고 connects the first child's identity to the second child's identity. The final past predicate supplies the past-time setting for both.
는 marks the other child as the contrasting topic.
The copula identifies the other child as Gildong.
-었- places the identification in the past narrative setting.
-습니다 closes the sentence in the formal polite narration style.
의 links Inhyeong to his mother: ‘Inhyeong's mother’. The shortened name 인형 retains the full-name identity 홍인형.
는 makes Inhyeong's mother the topic; the sentence identifies her as Lady Yu.
이다 connects the mother being discussed to her identity, Lady Yu.
The past form 이었다 identifies Inhyeong's mother within the story's past setting.
-습니다 finishes the past identification in the narration's formal polite style.
는 makes Lady Yu the topic; the sentence identifies her relationship to Minister Hong.
의 connects Minister Hong to 아내: Lady Yu was his wife.
The copula attaches to 아내 to identify Lady Yu as Minister Hong's wife.
The past form 였 places this marital relationship in the story's past.
습니다 ends the past statement in the narration's formal polite style.
의 connects Gildong to his mother: ‘Gildong's mother’. The shortened name 길동 retains the identity 홍길동.
는 makes Gildong's mother the topic; the sentence identifies her as Chunseom.
The copula identifies Gildong's mother as Chunseom.
었 places this identification in the past narrative: ‘was Chunseom’.
습니다 closes the identification in the formal polite style used by the narrator.
은 introduces Chunseom as the person whose work is being described.
의 connects Minister Hong to his household: 홍 판서의 집 means ‘Minister Hong's household’.
에서 marks the household as the place where Chunseom worked.
을 marks 일 as the object of 하다. 일을 하다 means ‘to work’.
하다 takes the past form 했-, showing that Chunseom did this work in the past.
-습니다 finishes the past statement in the formal polite style used by the narrator.
과 joins Inhyeong and Gildong as the two sons being compared.
의 applies to the coordinated names 인형과 길동: the father of both Inhyeong and Gildong.
는 presents their shared father as the topic, contrasting him with their different mothers.
았 places the shared-parent relationship in the past narrative: they had the same father.
지만 contrasts having the same father with having different mothers.
는 shifts the contrasting topic to their mothers. Korean does not require a plural marker here.
다르다 takes the irregular past form 달랐다, stating that the two boys had different mothers.
습니다 ends the past statement about their mothers in formal polite narration.
은 marks Inhyeong as the person this statement is about.
의 connects Gildong to 형: the older brother is Gildong's.
이다 identifies Inhyeong as Gildong's older brother.
었 places this family relationship in the story's past.
습니다 ends the narration as a formal polite statement.
이 marks Gildong as the person being born in the time clause.
-기 turns 태어나다 into the noun-like action ‘being born’, used before 전에.
-기 전에 places Minister Hong's dream before Gildong's birth.
에 follows 전 to mark the earlier time at which the dream occurred.
는 makes Minister Hong the topic of the main clause: he had the dream.
을 marks 꿈 as the object of 꾸다. 꿈을 꾸다 naturally means ‘have a dream’.
-었- places Minister Hong's dreaming in the past.
-습니다 gives the past statement the chapter's formal polite narrative style.
에서 marks the dream as the setting in which Minister Hong saw the dragon.
을 marks the dragon as what Minister Hong saw.
The past marker places seeing the dragon before the time of narration.
-습니다 presents the past action as a formal polite statement in the narration.
이 marks the dragon as the subject: the dragon came.
에게 marks Minister Hong as the person toward whom the dragon came.
오다 takes the past marker -았-, with 오았 contracting to 왔, to describe the dragon's arrival in the dream.
-습니다 ends the account of the dragon's arrival as a formal polite statement.
는 marks Minister Hong as the person whose feelings the sentence describes.
에서 marks sleep as the state Minister Hong emerges from when he wakes up; it means ‘from’ here.
일어난 modifies 후: the waking happens before the happiness described in the main clause.
에 marks 후 as the time when he was happy: after waking up.
일어난 후에 means ‘after waking up’. The completed-action modifier connects waking up to 후에.
기쁘다 becomes 기뻤다 to describe happiness at a past time; the stem vowel ㅡ drops in forming 기뻐.
The past predicate ends with 습니다 in the chapter's formal polite narrative style.
는 marks Minister Hong as the person whose thought is introduced.
했 expresses that Minister Hong thought at this point in the past narrative.
습니다 closes the narration in the formal polite statement style.
특별한 describes 아이: the child is special.
가 marks the child as the subject of the predicted birth.
태어나다 becomes 태어날 before 것 in the prediction.
태어날 것입니다 predicts that the child will be born. The formal polite ending occurs in Minister Hong's private thought.
이다 attaches to the dependent noun 것 within 태어날 것이다, meaning ‘will be born’. Together with the preceding modifier, 것이다 completes the prediction; it does not independently assert ‘is the case’.
것이다 becomes 것입니다 in formal polite style. 태어날 것입니다 still means ‘will be born’; the ending changes the speech style, not the predictive meaning.
에 marks 나중 as the later time when Chunseom lived with Minister Hong.
도 presents Chunseom as also living with Minister Hong.
와 marks Minister Hong as the person Chunseom lived with; 함께 reinforces the meaning ‘together’.
-았- places Chunseom's living with Minister Hong in the past.
-습니다 closes the narration as a formal polite statement.
은 introduces Chunseom as the topic and contrasts her position with Lady Yu's.
과 marks Lady Yu as the comparison partner for 같은; it means 'as' here rather than 'and' or 'with'.
같은 modifies 아내: a wife of the same kind or standing as Lady Yu.
는 contrasts the category 아내. Chunseom was not a wife with the same standing as Lady Yu.
유 부인과 같은 qualifies the category 아내 denied by 아니다. The contrastive 는 replaces the usual complement marker 가; the complete phrase denies being a wife of the same standing as Lady Yu.
grammar_links.display_meaning_en: was not a wife of the same standing as Lady Yu

grammar_links.context_en: 아니다 takes past marking to describe Chunseom's position at that time: 'was not'.
아니었습니다 ends the past negative statement in the formal polite style used by the narrator.
의 connects Chunseom to her social status: Chunseom's social status.
은 sets Chunseom's social status as the topic of the comparison.
보다 marks Lady Yu as the comparison point. Chunseom's social status was lower than Lady Yu's.
-았- places the lower social status in the past.
-습니다 ends this description in the narration's formal polite style.
의 links Chunseom to her son: ‘Chunseom's son’.
이 marks Gildong, identified as Chunseom's son, as the person who was born.
The past marker places Gildong's birth before the time of narration.
습니다 ends the account of his birth in formal polite narration.
는 makes the baby the topic: the statement describes what the baby was like.
했 places the baby's special quality in the past.
습니다 ends the description as a formal polite statement.
는 makes Minister Hong the topic: the sentence describes how he felt.
기쁘다 becomes 기뻤다 to describe happiness at that past moment.
-습니다 ends the past statement in the narration's formal polite style.
의 connects Gildong to his mother: ‘Gildong's mother’.
는 makes Gildong's mother the topic and contrasts her identity with Lady Yu.
이 marks Lady Yu as the identity denied by 아니었습니다: Gildong's mother was not Lady Yu.
The past marking places this denial of identity in the narrative's past.
-습니다 completes the negative statement in the narration's formal polite style.
는 marks Minister Hong as the topic of the statement.
The past marker places Minister Hong's happiness at this earlier point in the story. 기쁘다 becomes 기뻤다.
-지만 contrasts Minister Hong's happiness with the sadness he also felt.
은 marks his heart or feelings as a contrasting topic: despite his happiness, he felt sad inside.
The past marker describes his sadness at that time. 슬프다 becomes 슬펐다.
-습니다 closes the narration in the formal polite statement style; the sadness remains in the past.
이 marks time as what passed.
The past marker indicates that time passed before this point in the story.
습니다 ends the narration in a formal polite style.
은 makes Gildong the topic of the statement about his age.
이다 connects Gildong to the age expression 여덟 살, meaning eight years old.
The past marker places Gildong's age at this point in the story: he was eight years old.
-습니다 completes the age statement in the formal polite style used by the narrator.
은 sets Gildong as the topic: the sentence describes how he learned and studied.
-고 connects learning quickly with doing well at studying. The final past predicate 잘했습니다 places both actions in the past, so 배우고 here means ‘learned and’.
도 adds studying as another area in which Gildong did well, alongside learning quickly.
잘하- becomes 잘했- with the past marker, describing how well Gildong studied at that time.
-습니다 completes the past predicate as a formal polite narrative statement.
는 marks Gildong's father as the topic: the sentence describes his affection for Gildong.
을 marks Gildong as the person his father loved.
했 places the father's love in the past; 사랑하다 becomes 사랑했다.
습니다 ends the past statement in the narration's formal polite style.
의 connects Gildong to 생활: the life being described is Gildong's.
은 makes Gildong's life the topic, contrasting its difficulty with the preceding positive description.
-었- places the difficult circumstances of Gildong's life in the past.
-습니다 closes the description in the narration's formal polite style.
의 connects people with their social status: ‘people's social status’.
은 makes people's social status the topic of the statement.
같다 takes -지 to connect ‘be the same’ to the negative auxiliary 않다.
같지 않았습니다 denies sameness in the past. With 모두, the sentence says that people's social status was not the same for everyone.
-았- places the negative state in the story's past.
-습니다 ends the past negative statement in formal polite narration.
의 connects Minister Hong to his social status: Minister Hong's social status.
은 makes social status the topic; Minister Hong's high status contrasts with Chunseom's low status.
The past marker describes Minister Hong's social status at the time of the story.
습니다 ends the description of his high social status in formal polite narration.
의 connects Chunseom to her social status: ‘Chunseom's social status’.
은 makes Chunseom's social status the topic and contrasts it with Minister Hong's high status.
-았- places her low social status in the past setting of the story.
-습니다 ends the description in the chapter's formal polite narrative style.
은 sets Gildong as the topic: the sentence explains his social status.
의 connects Chunseom to 아들: Gildong is Chunseom's son.
The copula identifies Gildong as a son; 춘섬의 specifies whose son he is.
아들이라서 means 'because he was Chunseom's son': being her son explains his low social status. The main clause supplies the past narrative time.
이 marks social status as what was low.
았 places Gildong's low social status in the past narrative.
습니다 finishes the description of his low status in the chapter's formal polite narration.
에게 identifies Gildong as the person who has the family relationships expressed by 아버지와 형이 있었습니다: Gildong had a father and an older brother.
는 follows 에게 to make Gildong's situation the topic. The next sentence contrasts having a father and brother with being unable to address them by those titles.
와 joins 아버지 to 형: a father and an older brother.
이 marks the coordinated group 아버지와 형 as the people whose existence or family relationship is asserted by 있었습니다.
-었- places the existence of these family relationships in the past narrative. With 길동에게는, the sentence means Gildong had a father and an older brother.
-습니다 gives the past statement a formal polite ending without changing its meaning of having these family relationships.
를 marks his father as the person being addressed by a family title.
라고 marks ‘아버지’ as the exact title Gildong was not permitted to use when addressing his father.
부르다 becomes 부를 before the dependent noun 수; this modifier identifies the action whose possibility is denied.
부를 수 없었습니다 says that Gildong could not address his father as ‘Father’ because the social rules prohibited it, rather than because he lacked the ability to speak.
었 places the lack of permission in the past narrative.
습니다 closes the past statement in the chapter’s formal polite narrative style.
도 extends the same prohibition to his older brother: he could not address his brother by the family title either.
이라고 marks the quoted title 형 as what Gildong could not call his older brother.
부르다 becomes 부를 before 수 to present calling someone as a possible action.
부를 수 없었습니다 expresses that Gildong could not use this family title for his brother because his social position prevented it.
없었다 places the lack of permission or possibility in the past.
없었습니다 ends the past statement in the narration's formal polite style.
이 marks Gildong as the person who called his father by this title.
를 marks his father as the person being addressed.
라고 marks ‘아버지’ as the title Gildong used to address his father. The preceding word ends in a vowel, so the form is 라고.
부르다 becomes 불렀다 in the past: the 르 irregular change gives 불러-, followed by past marking. Gildong actually addressed his father as ‘Father’.
-습니다 ends the past-tense narration in a formal polite style; it does not change the meaning ‘called’.
는 makes his father the topic: the sentence tells what his father did.
에게 identifies Gildong as the person toward whom his father's anger was directed.
를 marks 화 as the object in 화를 내다, an expression meaning ‘get angry’ or ‘express anger’. Here his father became angry with Gildong.
내다 takes the past form 내었다, contracted to 냈다. In 화를 냈습니다, his father became angry with Gildong.
-습니다 finishes the past statement in the narration's formal polite style.
이 marks time as what passed.
The past marker places the passage of time before the narrative's current moment; 지나 contracts with 았 to form 지났-.
-습니다 completes the narration as a formal polite statement: more time passed.
은 makes Gildong the topic: the sentence tells us his age.
이 marks 열 살, ten years of age, as the threshold Gildong had passed; he was older than ten.
었 places Gildong's being over ten years old in the past.
습니다 ends the narration in the formal polite statement style.
를 marks his father as the person whom Gildong could not address by the quoted title.
라고 marks ‘아버지’ as the title Gildong could not use when addressing his father.
부르다 becomes 부를 before 수, presenting calling someone as a possible action.
부를 수 없었습니다 says Gildong could not use the title ‘Father’; the restriction comes from his social position.
The past marking places this inability at the time described in the story.
습니다 ends the past statement in the formal polite style used by the narrator.
도 adds his older brother to the family members Gildong could not address by their relationship titles: his older brother either.
이라고 marks ‘형’ as the quoted title Gildong could not use when addressing his older brother.
부르다 becomes 부를 before the dependent noun 수 in the expression of inability.
부를 수 없었습니다 expresses that Gildong could not use this title; the surrounding narrative establishes a social prohibition.
The past form places this inability in the narrated past.
-습니다 closes the sentence in the chapter's formal polite narrative style.
에서 marks the household as the place where the people worked.
이 marks 여러 사람, ‘several people’, as the subject doing the work. 사람 can refer to multiple people without 들.
을 marks 일 as the object of 하다. 일을 하다 means ‘to work’.
하다 becomes 했다 with past marking, placing the work before the time of narration.
했습니다 ends the past statement in the formal polite style used by the narrator.
들 makes explicit that several household workers are being discussed.
도 means that these people also looked down on Gildong, adding them to others who treated him as inferior.
의 connects Gildong to his social status: Gildong's status.
이 marks Gildong's social status as what was low in the reason clause.
낮아서 gives the reason the workers looked down on Gildong: his social status was low. The final past predicate establishes the past setting.
을 marks Gildong as the person the workers regarded as inferior.
-게 turns 낮다 into a description of their judgment. 낮게 보다 means to look down on someone or regard them as inferior, rather than physically looking downward.
-았- places the workers' judgment of Gildong in the past.
-습니다 gives the past narrative statement its formal polite ending.
의 connects Gildong to 마음: Gildong's heart or feelings.
은 makes Gildong's heart or feelings the topic of the description.
The past form 아팠- describes the emotional pain Gildong felt at this point in the story.
습니다 ends the description of his emotional pain in the narration's formal polite style.
The copula makes 밤 a predicate: it is night.
The past marker places this autumn night in the story's past.
The sentence ends in the formal polite style used in the narration.
은 makes Gildong the topic: the sentence tells what he was doing.
을 marks the book as what Gildong was reading.
-고 links 읽다 to the progressive auxiliary 있다, presenting reading as the action that continues.
The complete construction 읽고 있었습니다 describes reading as an action in progress at a past time.
-었- places the ongoing reading at a past time.
-습니다 gives the narration a formal polite statement ending.
이 marks 마음 as the subject: Gildong's heart or feelings were sad.
슬프다 becomes 슬펐다: the stem's ㅡ drops before -었-, expressing that he felt sad at that time.
-습니다 ends the past description in the narration's formal polite style.
은 marks Gildong as the topic: the sentence tells what he did.
했 places Gildong's speaking in the past.
습니다 ends the narration in a formal polite style.
는 marks Gildong as the topic as he states his own wish.
를 marks the country as what Gildong wants to help.
-고 links 돕다 to the auxiliary 싶다, identifying helping as the desired action.
The complete construction expresses Gildong's wish to help his country.
-습니다 presents Gildong's wish as a formal polite statement in present time.
의 connects 나라 to 일: work concerning the country, here serving the country.
을 marks 일 as the work the speaker wants to do well.
-고 connects 잘하다 to the auxiliary 싶다 to express wanting to do well.
잘하고 싶습니다 expresses the speaker's wish to do the country's work well.
-습니다 makes the statement of desire formal and polite; it does not add past tense.
들 explicitly marks more than one person: the people Gildong wants to know his name.
에게 marks the people to whom Gildong wants to make his name known.
내 is the contraction of 나의, meaning ‘my’; it identifies the name as Gildong's own.
도 adds making his name known to his previously expressed wishes to help the country and do its work well. It replaces the object marker on 이름.
-고 links 알리다 to the auxiliary 싶다, identifying making known as the desired action.
알리고 싶습니다 expresses Gildong's own wish to make his name known to people.
-습니다 ends Gildong's statement of desire in the formal polite style.
는 marks Gildong himself as the topic: as for him, he is alone despite having a father and brother.
이다 makes 혼자 a predicate describing the speaker as alone.
입니다 ends Gildong's statement that he is alone in the formal polite style.
도 includes his father among the family members he has; the matching 도 on 형 adds his older brother.
-고 connects having a father with having an older brother. Here 있다 expresses having a family relationship.
도 means he also has an older brother, in addition to his father.
-습니다 ends Gildong's statement formally and politely. 있습니다 expresses that he has an older brother.
는 makes Gildong himself the topic: he is asking about the restriction placed on him.
를 marks his father as the person whom he wants to address by a family title.
라고 marks ‘아버지’ as the exact title used with 부르다: to call someone ‘Father’.
부르다 becomes 부를 before 수, presenting calling him by that title as a possible action.
부를 수 없습니까 asks why Gildong cannot call his father ‘Father’. The impossibility here comes from a social restriction, rather than an inability to speak.
-습니까 makes 없다 a formal polite question. Together with 왜, the sentence asks why this action is not possible.
을 marks the older brother as the person Gildong wants to address.
이라고 marks ‘형’ as the exact family title Gildong is forbidden to use when addressing his older brother.
부를 modifies 수, identifying calling someone by a title as the action whose possibility is being questioned.
부를 수 없습니까 asks why Gildong cannot call his older brother ‘형’; the inability comes from the social prohibition.
grammar_links.display_meaning_en: can I not call him that?

grammar_links.context_en: -습니까 turns 없다 into a formal polite question. Here Gildong asks himself why he cannot use the family title while speaking alone.
이 marks 마음 as what hurts. Gildong is describing his emotional pain.
아픕니다 is the formal polite statement form of 아프다. Here it describes emotional pain in the present.
은 makes Gildong the topic: the sentence tells what he did.
으로 marks 밖 as the direction of Gildong's movement: outside.
The contracted past form 나갔- places Gildong's going out before the time of narration.
-습니다 ends the past-tense statement in the formal polite narration style.
을 marks the sword as what Gildong held.
들고 connects the actions: Gildong held the sword and practiced. The final 했습니다 supplies past time for both actions; -고 itself does not mark past tense.
을 marks 연습 as the activity performed with 하다; 연습을 하다 means to practice.
하다 becomes 했다, placing the practice in the past.
했습니다 presents the past action as a formal polite statement.
도 adds Father to the people outside: Father was outside too.
에 marks outside as the place where Father was.
-었- places Father's being outside in the past.
-습니다 ends the narration in a formal polite style.
는 makes his father the topic: the sentence tells what his father did.
을 marks Gildong as the person his father saw. Gildong is also the understood person he called to.
보고 connects seeing Gildong with calling to him. The past ending on 불렀습니다 places both actions in the past, so 보고 here means ‘saw him and’.
부르다 becomes 불렀다 with the past ending: his father called to Gildong. The 르 irregular change produces 불러 before contraction with the past ending.
습니다 ends the past statement in the narration's formal polite style.
이 marks 밤 as the subject: the night has grown late.
-었- is past morphology, but here 늦었다 describes the resulting current state: the hour has grown late.
-습니다 presents the father's statement about the current late hour in a formal polite style.
안 negates 자다, ‘sleep’. With 왜 아직, the father asks why Gildong is still not sleeping.
The vowel-ending stem 자- takes -ㅂ니까 to form 잡니까, ‘are you sleeping?’, a formal polite question.
이 marks Gildong as the person who answered.
했 places Gildong's answer in the past.
-습니다 ends the narration in a formal polite style.
도 adds ‘too’: Gildong asserts that he, like other people, is a person.
The copula connects the speaker to 사람: ‘I am a person.’
입니다 is the formal polite statement form of the copula, used while addressing his father.
는 marks the humble pronoun 저 as the topic: Gildong contrasts himself with other people.
과 marks other people as the comparison partner of 같다: being the same as other people.
-지 connects 같다 to 않다; the following auxiliary supplies the negation.
같지 않습니까 asks why Gildong is not the same as other people. The negative construction includes both 같지 and 않습니까.
-습니까 ends the negative predicate as a formal polite question addressed to his father.
는 makes the respectful pronoun 저 the topic: Gildong asks about his own treatment.
도 means ‘even’ here. With 아니다, Gildong asks why he is not treated as even a person.
사람 is the identity denied by 아니다. The emphatic particle 도 replaces the usual complement marker 이/가, giving ‘not even a person’.
grammar_links.display_meaning_en: am I not even a person?

grammar_links.context_en: 아니다 takes -ㅂ니까 to form a respectful question denying an identity: ‘am I not?’
는 establishes the father as the topic: he understood Gildong's feelings.
의 connects Gildong to 마음: the feelings are Gildong's.
을 marks Gildong's feelings as what his father understood.
-았- places the father's understanding of Gildong's feelings in the past.
-습니다 ends the narrator's statement in a formal polite style.
에게 marks Gildong as the person toward whom his father's anger is directed.
를 marks 화 as the object of 내다. Together, 화를 내다 means to express anger or get angry, rather than literally put anger outside.
내다 takes the past form 내었다, contracted to 냈다. His father expressed anger again.
-습니다 ends this past-tense narrative statement in a formal polite style.
이다 makes 말 the predicate. Together with 무슨, the father asks what Gildong means by his words.
The copula takes the formal polite question form 입니까. The whole question naturally means ‘What do you mean?’
은 marks Gildong as the person this statement is about.
에서 marks where Gildong spoke: in front of his father. 아버지 앞 means the space in front of his father.
했 places Gildong's speaking in the past; 말하다 becomes 말했다.
습니다 ends the narration as a formal polite statement; 말했습니다 means 'spoke'.
는 marks Gildong, speaking humbly as 저, as the topic: he is grateful to his parents.
에게 marks the people toward whom Gildong feels gratitude: his parents.
-습니다 makes Gildong's statement of gratitude formal and polite.
는 marks the humble pronoun 저 as the topic: Gildong is describing how he himself feels.
-ㅂ니다 makes 슬프다 a formal polite statement as Gildong speaks respectfully to his father.
제 is the contracted form of 저의, meaning ‘my’ in respectful speech; it identifies the father as the speaker's father.
가 marks the speaker's father as the person whose location is stated.
에 marks 앞 as the location where the father is: in front of the speaker.
-습니다 ends the statement about the father's present location in a formal polite style.
는 makes the respectful pronoun 저 the topic: Gildong contrasts having a father with his own inability to address him as Father.
를 marks 아버지 as the person Gildong cannot call by the quoted title.
라고 marks the preceding quoted 아버지 as the title used in calling someone, rather than identifying another person.
부르다 becomes 부를 before the dependent noun 수; this modifier prepares the action for the following possibility construction.
부를 수 없습니다 means that Gildong cannot use the address Father; the impossibility comes from the social prohibition.
-습니다 ends the negative possibility statement in formal polite speech to his father. It does not add past tense.
도 extends the same restriction to his older brother: he cannot address his brother by the family title either.
이라고 marks ‘형’ as the title he is unable to use when addressing his older brother.
부를 is the modifier form of 부르다 required before 수 in the expression of inability.
부를 수 없습니다 expresses the restriction preventing him from calling his older brother ‘형’.
-습니다 ends the statement of inability in a formal polite style.
은 marks Gildong as the person this statement is about.
-었- places Gildong's crying in the past.
-습니다 ends the narration in a formal polite style.
의 connects Father to his heart or feelings: ‘Father's heart’.
도 indicates that Father also felt emotional pain, as Gildong did.
아팠다 places Father's emotional pain in the past; 아프다 describes hurt feelings here.
-습니다 ends the past description of Father's feelings in the narration's formal polite style.
는 sets his father as the topic of the statement about worrying.
했 marks his father's worrying as occurring in the past.
습니다 ends the narrator's statement in a formal polite style.
Marks Gildong as the person to whom his father might say kind words.
좋은 describes the following 말: good or kind words.
Marks the words as what the father might say in 말을 하다.
Introduces the father's imagined condition: if he says kind words to Gildong now.
Marks a later time when Gildong might stop heeding his father's words.
Marks Gildong as the subject of the possible failure to listen.
내 is the contraction of 나의, meaning 'my'; it identifies the words as the father's.
Marks the father's words as what Gildong might fail to heed.
안 negates 듣다, here meaning to listen to or heed someone's words. The father wonders whether Gildong might not heed him later.
The father asks himself about an uncertain consequence. 듣다 changes its stem from 듣- to 들- before -을까; the preceding 안 makes the question negative.
는 marks Gildong's father as the person this statement is about.
에게 identifies Gildong as the person toward whom his father's anger is directed.
를 marks 화 as the object of 내다. Together, 화를 내다 means to get angry or express anger.
내다 takes the past form 내었다, contracted to 냈다. The father expressed anger at this point in the story.
-습니다 gives the past statement a formal polite ending.
에 marks the households where a child like Gildong exists.
도 adds other households to Gildong's household: they too have a child in a similar situation.
와 marks 너 as the person the other child is compared with: a child like you.
같은 modifies 아이, describing a child whose situation is similar to Gildong's.
가 marks 아이 as the child whose presence in another household is stated.
있습니다 states that such a child exists, using a formal polite ending.
의 connects the child to his or her mother: ‘that child's mother’.
도 means that this child's mother also has low social status, like Gildong's mother.
이 marks social status as what is described as low.
-습니다 ends the description of the mother's social status as a formal polite statement.
은 makes what Gildong said the topic of his father's rejection.
안 negates 됩니다 in its acceptability sense: his father says that what Gildong said is not acceptable.
-ㅂ니다 ends the statement in a formal polite style; 됩니다 is the formal polite form of 되다.
Here -고 connects 듣다 to 싶다 to express wanting to hear; it does not mean ‘and’.
듣고 싶다 means ‘want to hear’. The following 지 않습니다 negates this desire: the father does not want to hear such words again.
-지 connects 싶다 to 않다, allowing the desire to be negated.
싶지 않습니다 means ‘do not want to’. The negation applies to wanting, rather than expressing inability to hear.
-습니다 ends the father's negative statement in a formal polite style.
은 marks Gildong as the person the statement is about.
대답할 modifies 수, presenting answering as a possible action.
The complete construction states that Gildong could not answer.
었 places the inability to answer in the past.
습니다 ends the narration in a formal polite style.
The past marker -었- places Gildong's crying in the past.
-습니다 closes the narration as a formal polite statement.
는 makes his father the topic: the sentence tells what his father said.
에게 marks Gildong as the person his father spoke to.
했 places the speaking in the past: his father said something.
습니다 ends the narrator's statement in a formal polite style.
The ending -세요 makes this a polite command. Here the father tells Gildong to leave; it is a dismissal rather than an invitation.
은 marks Gildong as the topic: the sentence tells what he did.
으로 marks the room as the destination of Gildong's return.
The past marker in 돌아갔습니다 places Gildong's return before the time of narration.
-습니다 ends the statement about Gildong's return in the narration's formal polite style.
은 makes Gildong's feelings the topic, contrasting his continuing sadness with his return to his room.
The past form describes how Gildong felt after returning to his room. 슬프다 becomes 슬펐다 with the past ending.
-습니다 closes the past description in the chapter's formal polite narrative style.

beats.event_en: Minister Hong lives in Joseon and has two sons. Inhyeong is the son of his wife, Lady Yu; Gildong is the son of Chunseom, a woman serving in the household.
beats.quote: 화셜 됴션국 셰종됴 시졀의 ᄒᆞᆫ ᄌᆡ샹이 이시니 셩은 홍이오 명은 뫼라. ᄃᆡᄃᆡ 명문거죡으로 쇼년 등과ᄒᆞ여 벼ᄉᆞᆯ이 니죠판셔의 니르ᄆᆡ, 물망이 됴야의 읏듬이오, 츙효 겸비ᄒᆞ기로 일홈이 일국의 진동ᄒᆞ더라. 일즉 두 아들을 두어시니, 일ᄌᆞᄂᆞᆫ 일홈이 인형이니 뎡실 뉴시 쇼ᄉᆡᆼ이오, 일ᄌᆞᄂᆞᆫ 일홈이 길동이니 시비 츈셤의 쇼ᄉᆡᆼ이라.

beats.event_en: Before Gildong's birth, Minister Hong dreams that a blue dragon rushes toward him. He wakes happily and believes the dream means he will have an exceptional child.
beats.quote: 션시의 공이 길동을 나흘 ᄯᆡ의 일몽을 어드니, 문득 뇌졍벽녁이 진동ᄒᆞ며 쳥룡이 슈염을 거ᄉᆞ리고 공의게 향ᄒᆞ여 다라들거ᄂᆞᆯ, 놀나 ᄭᆡ다르니 일쟝츈몽이라. 심즁의 ᄃᆡ희ᄒᆞ여 ᄉᆡᆨ각ᄒᆞ되, ‘ᄂᆡ 이졔 룡몽을 어더시니 반ᄃᆞ시 귀ᄒᆞᆫ 자식을 나흐리라’ ᄒᆞ고 즉시 ᄂᆡ당으로 드러가니, 부인 뉴시 니러 맛거ᄂᆞᆯ, 공이 흔언이 그 옥슈를 니그러 졍이 친압고져 ᄒᆞ거ᄂᆞᆯ, 부인이 졍ᄉᆡᆨ 왈,

beats.event_en: Chunseom becomes Minister Hong's concubine and gives birth to an exceptional-looking boy. Minister Hong is happy but regrets that the child was not born to his wife.
beats.quote: ᄒᆞ고, 언파의 손을 ᄯᅥᆯ치고 나가거ᄂᆞᆯ, 공이 가쟝 무류ᄒᆞ여 분긔ᄅᆞᆯ ᄎᆞᆷ지 못ᄒᆞ고 외당의 나와 부인의 지식이 업스물 한탄ᄒᆞ더니, 맛ᄎᆞᆷ 시비 츈셤이 ᄎᆞᄅᆞᆯ 올니긔로 그 고요ᄒᆞ믈 인ᄒᆞ여 츈셤을 잇글고 협실의 드러가 졍이 친압ᄒᆞ니, 이 ᄯᆡ 츈셤의 나히 십팔이라. ᄒᆞᆫ 번 몸을 허ᄒᆞᆫ 후로 문외의 나지 아니ᄒᆞ고 타인을 ᄎᆔᄒᆞᆯ ᄯᅳᆺ이 업스니, 공이 긔특이 넉여 인ᄒᆞ여 잉쳡을 삼아더니, 과연 그 달붓허 ᄐᆡ긔 잇셔 십 삭만의 일ᄀᆡ 옥동을 ᄉᆡᆼᄒᆞ니, 긔골이 비범ᄒᆞ여 진짓 영웅 호걸의 긔상이라. 공이 일변 깃거ᄒᆞ나 부인의게 나지 못ᄒᆞ믈 한ᄒᆞ더라.

beats.event_en: Gildong grows into a quick learner, and his father loves him increasingly. Because of his mother's low status, he is scolded when he calls his father father or his brother older brother. Even after he turns ten, he cannot use those forms of address; the servants also mistreat him. One autumn night, he pushes aside his reading desk and speaks about his sorrow.
beats.quote: 길동이 졈졈 ᄌᆞ라 팔 셰 되ᄆᆡ, 춍명이 과인ᄒᆞ여 ᄒᆞᆫ아흘 드르면 ᄇᆡᆨ을 통ᄒᆞ니 공이 더옥 ᄋᆡ즁ᄒᆞ나, 근본 쳔ᄉᆡᆼ이라 길동이 ᄆᆡ양 호부호형ᄒᆞ면 문득 ᄭᅮ지져 못ᄒᆞ계 ᄒᆞ니, 길동이 십 셰 넘도록 감히 부형을 부르지 못ᄒᆞ고, 비복 등이 쳔ᄃᆡᄒᆞ물 각골통한ᄒᆞ여 심ᄉᆞᄅᆞᆯ 졍치 못ᄒᆞ더니, 츄구월 망간을 당ᄒᆞᄆᆡ, 명월은 죠요ᄒᆞ고 쳥풍은 쇼슬ᄒᆞ여 사ᄅᆞᆷ의 심회ᄅᆞᆯ 돕ᄂᆞᆫ지라. 길동이 셔당의셔 글을 닑다가 문득 셔안을 밀치고 탄왈,

beats.event_en: Gildong wishes to accomplish great things for his country and make his name known. He feels lonely and deeply hurt because he has a father and an older brother but cannot call them by those family titles.
beats.quote: “대쟝뷔 셰샹의 나ᄆᆡ 공ᄆᆡᆼ을 본밧지 못ᄒᆞ면, 찰아리 병법을 외와 대쟝닌을 요하의 빗기 ᄎᆞ고 동졍셔벌ᄒᆞ여, 국가의 ᄃᆡ공을 셰우고 일홈을 만ᄃᆡ의 빗ᄂᆡ미 쟝부의 쾌ᄉᆡ라. 나ᄂᆞᆫ 엇지ᄒᆞ여 일신이 젹막ᄒᆞ고 부형이 이시되 호부호형을 못ᄒᆞ니 심쟝이 터질지라. 엇지 통한치 아니리오.”

beats.event_en: Gildong goes into the courtyard to practice swordsmanship. His father, who is also outside looking at the moon, sees him and calls him over.
beats.quote: ᄒᆞ고, 말을 맛츠며 ᄯᅳᆯ의 나려 검술을 공부ᄒᆞ더니, 맛ᄎᆞᆷ 공이 ᄯᅩᄒᆞᆫ 월ᄉᆡᆨ을 구경ᄒᆞ다가 길동의 ᄇᆡ회ᄒᆞ믈 보고 즉시 불너 문왈,

beats.event_en: His father asks why he is still awake so late at night.
beats.quote: “네 무ᄉᆞᆷ 흥이 이셔 야심토록 잠을 ᄌᆞ지 아니ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ다?”

beats.event_en: His father asks what he means.
Gildong explains that he is grateful to his parents, yet his lasting sorrow is that he cannot call his own father father or his older brother older brother.
beats.quote: “쇼인이 평ᄉᆡᆼ 셜운 바ᄂᆞᆫ, 대감 졍긔로 당당ᄒᆞ온 남ᄌᆡ 되여ᄉᆞ오니 부ᄉᆡᆼ모휵지은이 깁ᄉᆞᆸ거ᄂᆞᆯ, 그 부친을 부친이라 못ᄒᆞ옵고, 그 형을 형이라 못ᄒᆞ오니 엇지 사ᄅᆞᆷ이라 ᄒᆞ오리잇가.”

beats.event_en: His father says Gildong is not the only child in such a household whose mother has low status and warns him never to raise this complaint again.
beats.quote: “ᄌᆡ샹가 쳔비 쇼ᄉᆡᆼ이 비단 너ᄲᅮᆫ이 아니거든, 네 엇지 방ᄌᆞᄒᆞ미 이 ᄀᆞᆺ흐뇨. ᄎᆞ후 다시 이런 말이 이시면 안젼의 용납지 못ᄒᆞ리라.”

beats.event_en: Gildong cannot answer and continues crying. His father tells him to leave, and Gildong returns to his room still deeply sad.
beats.quote: ᄒᆞ니, 길동이 감이 일언을 고치 못ᄒᆞ고 다만 복지유쳬 ᄲᅮᆫ이라. 공이 명ᄒᆞ여 물너가라 하거ᄂᆞᆯ, 길동이 침쇼로 도라와 슬허ᄒᆞ믈 마지 아이ᄒᆞ더라.

entries.role_en: Gildong and Inhyeong's father, identified by his surname and official title in the reviewed source notes.
Son of Minister Hong and Chunseom; forbidden to address his father and older half-brother by their family titles because of his mother's low status.
Son of Minister Hong and his wife, Lady Yu; Gildong's older half-brother.
Minister Hong's wife and Inhyeong's mother; distinct from Gildong's mother, Chunseom.

The sole essential story-term exemption: expresses the inherited social distinction underlying Gildong's unequal treatment and the prohibition on addressing his father and older brother by their family titles.

adaptation_decisions.scope_reason_en: Cover the contiguous opening through paragraph 16: introduce Minister Hong and his two sons with their different mothers, retain the dragon dream and Gildong's birth, show his intelligence and the unequal treatment he receives, and develop the nighttime conversation with his father through its painful conclusion. These events can support a substantial chapter in short, natural beginner sentences without reducing the scene to a summary. Explain the family relationships directly; refer to the father by his reviewed title, never by the placeholder as a personal name. Simplify official rank, social status and Gildong's ambitions into concrete language. Omit the intimate encounter, Lady Yu's rebuke, pregnancy chronology, classical exemplars, military insignia and decorative moonlight imagery because they add difficulty without being necessary to understand this scene. Preserve the father's affection alongside his refusal to allow family forms of address, and distinguish the servants' mistreatment from the father's restrictions. Paragraph 16 completes the confrontation as Gildong returns to his room in sadness. More narrative is adaptable, but paragraph 17 begins a separate conversation with his mother about leaving home and leads toward the household plot; reserve that development for the next chapter, beginning immediately at paragraph 17.
adaptation_decisions.length_reason_en: This chapter covers the reviewed opening through paragraph 16, retaining the family relationships, dragon dream, birth, learning ability, unequal treatment, ambitions and complete nighttime confrontation. Chunseom's subsequent relationship with Minister Hong is expressed as living with him while explicitly distinguishing her family position from that of his wife, Lady Yu; lower social status is stated separately. This avoids presenting the women as equivalent wives and introduces no second story-term exemption. Short, connected sentences preserve substantial narrative development without a length quota or invented padding. Intimate details, pregnancy chronology, classical exemplars, military insignia, decorative moonlight imagery and the desk movement are omitted because their incidental difficulty would outweigh their contribution at this level. Paragraph 16 provides a coherent conclusion: the father dismisses Gildong, who returns to his room still sad. More meaningful source narrative can be adapted, but paragraph 17 begins the separate conversation with his mother and is reserved for the next chapter. 신분 remains the sole planned story term. Future prediction, quoted forms of address and the conditional thought still require their actual curriculum bindings and optional-learning assessment; lexical-budget acceptance and independent curriculum approval remain subsequent review tasks.

bindings.level_reason_en: The chapter remains suitable for supported Level 1 reading. Short statements, familiar family vocabulary, past narration and Level 1 possibility, desire and negation constructions carry most of the story. The Level 3 quotation particle repeats in the same concrete frame about calling someone ‘Father’ or ‘older brother’. Understanding the central restriction depends on this pattern, so its occurrences need contextual support. Level 2 modifiers mostly appear in short noun phrases or within familiar Level 1 constructions. The single conditional adds a modest demand in the father's private thought. The unlisted prediction, adverbial formation and plural marker have limited scope; short negation is natural beginner wording despite the catalog gap. These exceptions do not dominate the chapter or require varied advanced clause structures. Ordinary above-level vocabulary still requires the publication occurrence-budget check; names and the planned 신분 exemption remain separate.
